title: Pack the Bag
story: An explorer's bag holds a map and a rope. A torch is missing.
goal: Add "torch" to the end of bag, then print how many items it holds and the first item.
starter:
bag = ["map", "rope"]
# add "torch" to the end of the bag
# then print the number of items, then the first item

tests.label: bag is now map, rope, torch

hints: Lists have an append method: bag.append(...) adds one item at the end.
len(bag) counts items. The first item is bag[0] because counting starts at zero.
socratic: Which list method adds an item to the end?
Which function tells you how many items a list has?
What index is the first item?
explain: In one sentence: why is the first item at index 0?

example.title: Worked example: a fruit list
example.note: Lists are ordered, start at index 0, and grow with append.
